methodology_note: Reliability ratings are qualitative summaries of independent third-party media evaluators (Ad Fontes Media's Media Bias Chart, Media Bias/Fact Check, AllSides), not scores invented by this project. They describe track record for factual accuracy, not agreement with any political viewpoint. Re-check periodically -- outlets can and do change over time.

publishers.name: BBC News
publishers.funding_model: Public broadcaster funded by the UK license fee; editorial independence set out in its Royal Charter.

reliability.note: Long-running wire-style reporting with minimal detectable lean on straight news.

publishers.name: NPR
publishers.funding_model: Nonprofit member organization; funded by member station fees, sponsorships and listener donations rather than a single owner.

reliability.note: Strong factual track record; MBFC notes a slight left-leaning story-selection bias on some coverage.

publishers.name: PBS NewsHour
publishers.funding_model: Nonprofit public broadcasting, funded by federal/state grants, viewer donations and corporate sponsorship -- no single commercial owner.

reliability.note: Consistently rated near the top for factual reporting with minimal detectable lean.

publishers.name: Deutsche Welle (DW)
publishers.funding_model: Germany's state-funded international broadcaster; independence from government influence is set by the Deutsche Welle Act.

reliability.note: Useful for a non-US/UK vantage point on the same stories.

publishers.name: Al Jazeera English
publishers.funding_model: Funded by the Qatari state; operates with substantial day-to-day editorial autonomy but this ownership link is worth surfacing to readers, not hiding.

reliability.note: Valuable for Middle East and Global South coverage often under-reported elsewhere.

publishers.name: The Christian Science Monitor
publishers.funding_model: Nonprofit-backed newspaper; explicitly avoids sensationalism as an editorial policy.

reliability.note: Rated 'least biased' by MBFC; known for calm, low-sensationalism reporting.

publishers.name: ProPublica
publishers.funding_model: Nonprofit investigative newsroom funded by grants and reader donations, not advertising or a single proprietor.

reliability.note: Investigative, evidence-heavy reporting; multiple Pulitzer Prizes for accuracy-critical work.

publishers.name: The Guardian
publishers.funding_model: Owned by the Scott Trust, a structure created specifically to preserve editorial independence from commercial or political owners.

reliability.note: Strong factual reporting on news pages; MBFC notes a left-of-center lean in framing/opinion content.

publishers.name: Reuters
publishers.funding_model: Global wire service; part of Thomson Reuters. Reuters retired its public RSS feeds in 2020.

reliability.note: Included in the publisher list for completeness. No free RSS is available -- fetch_news.py skips it until a paid API or licensed feed is wired in.

publishers.name: Associated Press (AP)
publishers.funding_model: Nonprofit news cooperative owned by its member newspapers and broadcasters.

reliability.note: Included for completeness. No free public RSS -- same status as Reuters, needs a paid API or licensed feed.
